newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil soluble coffee makers agree to delay import.
newsitem.headline: Brazil soluble coffee makers agree to delay import.

text.p: Brazil's soluble coffee industry wants to import robusta coffee to alleviate a supply shortage but has agreed to a government request to wait a little longer, a soluble industry spokesman said.
"The soluble coffee industry wants to import but the government is asking for calm," said a spokesman for Brazil's Soluble Coffee Industry Association (Abics).
Soluble coffee producers claim they are losing market share to overseas competitors because the current high price of raw materials in Brazil makes them less competitive.

Brazil's coffee council, known as the CDPC, has been discussing the possibility of lending the soluble industry up to 770,000 60-kg bags of poorer-quality government stocks, repayable in kind over three years.
However, the proposal has still to be approved by the National Monetary Council, the country's highest economic authority.
At the moment, the plan is at a standstill and soluble coffee producers may resort to imports soon, the spokesman said.
"Everything is paralyzed," he said. "I think within a short time period the soluble industry will import."
At a preliminary meeting of the CDPC council Tuesday, the Industry and Commerce Ministry again asked Abics to postpone the move, the spokesman added.

The soluble industry earlier this year planned to import robusta coffee from India but held off at the government's request, he noted. But if it decided to go ahead with the purchase, it would not necessarily buy from India, he said.
"It could be from any market. Once you get into the market, it's a very agile process," the spokesman said.
The CDPC was scheduled to hold another preliminary meeting Thursday ahead of its next formal session, for which no date has yet been set.
